sections.h2: Who sends the Carrollton property tax bill
sections.html:
A county tax office does, and which one depends on where your house sits, because Carrollton lies in Dallas, Denton and Collin counties. The Dallas County Tax Office bills Dallas County parcels, and the Denton County Tax Office bills parcels in both Denton and Collin counties. Statements go out in October, and they do not come from the City of Carrollton.

Value is set separately. The Dallas, Denton and Collin central appraisal districts each value the parcels in their county and hear protests. If you are unsure which county holds your lot, check the property address on an old statement or use the appraisal district search.

The City Council adopted $0.537000 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2027, which began October 1. The city's news release calls it the lowest rate since 1989 and the 13th straight annual cut, down from $0.537500. The city also kept its senior and disabled exemptions at $110,000.

The average homestead market value is $419,401 and the average taxable value is $339,580, with the 20 percent homestead exemption and value caps applied. The city is only one line on the bill. The school district, county and special districts add their own rates, shown below for fiscal year 2026.

Three school districts serve Carrollton: Carrollton-Farmers Branch, Lewisville and Dallas ISD. If your house is on the Collin side, ask the Denton County Tax Office or the Collin Central Appraisal District for the Collin County rate.

For the average Carrollton homestead, each dollar of property tax splits like this: $0.59 to the school district, $0.30 to the city and $0.11 to the county. The school share funds schools and operations. The city share pays for police, fire, streets, the library, parks, development, environmental work and animal control. The county share covers county roads, sheriff services, courts and health and human services.

The tax rate has two parts, maintenance and operations plus debt, and the Council sets it with the budget in August. A separate stormwater fee began October 1, 2026 on utility bills. About 80 percent of residential properties land in Tier 2 at $7.25. It is a utility charge, not a property tax.

Taxes become payable October 1 and turn delinquent if unpaid by January 31. Late charges work like this:

  • A 6% penalty on the first day of the month of delinquency, rising 1% a month until July 1, when it becomes 12%
  • Interest of 1% at the start, then 1% more each month
  • An added penalty of up to 20% of taxes, penalties and interest if the tax is still unpaid on July 1

Texas also allows a split payment: half by November 30 and half by June 30, with a written request to waive penalty and interest. Homeowners 65 or older or disabled may pay in four installments. Ask the county tax office which option you qualify for before you count on it.

Pay the county office that bills your parcel. Each office takes mail, online and in-person payments.

  • Dallas County parcels: mail to the Dallas County Tax Assessor-Collector, 500 Elm St., Dallas, TX 75202, or pay in person at the North Dallas location, 6820 LBJ Freeway, Suite 1300, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Phone 214-653-7811.
  • Denton and Collin parcels: mail to the Denton County Tax Assessor-Collector, 1505 E. McKinney Street, Denton, TX 76209-4525, or pay in person at the Carrollton location, 1029 W. Rosemeade Parkway, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Phone 940-349-3500.
  • Online payments carry fees, and both offices accept cards and echeck.

sections.h2: How to lower a Carrollton tax bill
sections.html:
File for every exemption you qualify for, and protest the value if you think it is too high. The city offers a 20 percent homestead exemption, a $110,000 exemption for owners 65 or older, a $110,000 exemption for disabled persons and a disabled veterans exemption. You file with the appraisal district, never with the city. Exemptions filed by May 1 appear on the original statement, and later filings produce a supplemental bill.

School districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, plus $60,000 more for homeowners 65 or older or disabled. For a protest, the deadline is May 15, or the 30th day after delivery of the notice when that is later. Appraisal notices usually arrive in April, and the appraisal district, not the city, hears the case.

sections.h2: Selling with this year's tax unpaid
sections.html:
Value and ownership are fixed as of January 1, and the tax lien attaches on that date. The bill for the year arrives in October, after many spring and summer sales have closed. Ask the closing agent how the year's tax will be split between you and the buyer.

If you owe back taxes, penalties keep growing until July 1. Ask the title company for a payoff figure from the county tax office rather than estimating, and do not rely on a number from a prior year's statement.

Carrollton had 134,562 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up from 133,434 in 2020, on 36.66 square miles. Owners occupy 58.5% of 51,995 households. The median owner-occupied home value is $381,000 for 2020 to 2024, and median gross rent is $1,735. That survey median differs from the city's $419,401 average homestead market value, so the two figures will not match.

faqs.q: Which county tax office do I pay if my house is in Carrollton?
faqs.a: It depends on the county where the parcel sits. Dallas County parcels go to the Dallas County Tax Office, and Denton and Collin County parcels go to the Denton County Tax Office.

faqs.q: What is the Carrollton city property tax rate for fiscal year 2027?
faqs.a: $0.537000 per $100 of assessed value, lowered from $0.537500. The city calls it the lowest rate since 1989. School, county and special district rates are added on top.

faqs.q: When do Carrollton property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31. Taxes are payable from October 1, and a 6% penalty plus 1% interest start the month after the deadline. The penalty reaches 12% on July 1.

faqs.q: Does the City of Carrollton handle appraisal protests?
faqs.a: No. The Dallas, Denton and Collin central appraisal districts hear protests and approve exemptions. File by May 15 or within 30 days of delivery of the appraisal notice, whichever is later.

A 20 percent homestead exemption, a $110,000 exemption for owners 65 or older, a $110,000 exemption for disabled persons and a disabled veterans exemption. File with the appraisal district for your county.
